facts.fact: Klaaren and Costa, as reported by the op-ed, found the state enlisted private commercial banks to handle identity enrolment and verification for South Africa's digital identity framework.
facts.system: Home Affairs Smart ID verification via banks

ZAF.note: Document says nothing on links between the civil register and the ID system.
Document mentions no civil service digital-skills training in South Africa (Kerala training is another country).
No rural internet programme or rural/urban use figures stated.
No public digital-skills programme or measured share stated.
No enrolment count or share stated.
Dependency on vendors is argued in general terms; no statement on who operates or maintains the national ID system.
No public register keyed on the ID number stated.

facts.fact: The op-ed describes a client renewing a Smart ID card with biometric capture at a bank branch in Sandton, and South Africa's move from Hanis to the facial-recognition-equipped Abis, per Klaaren and Costa.

ZAF.note: Only a general claim that skilled engineers left government and procurement failed; no named body or system stated.
Mentions high data tariffs only for the Sahel, with no price.
No account or payment survey figure stated.
